Reverie re-baselined at v1.0.0 but the repo (renamed from codexCLI, not forked) still carried codexCLI's git tags v0.1.0–v1.14.0 — so Reverie's v1.x line COLLIDED with old tags on every release. Resolved 2026-06-08 during the v1.1.0 cut: purged all 36 pre-rebrand tags (v0.x and v1.1.0–v1.14.0, none had GitHub Releases) from local + origin, kept only v1.0.0 (the launch, has a Release). Reverie's 1.x line is now collision-free. Commits stay in history (untagged). If a future audit finds stale tags reappear, they were likely re-fetched from a stale clone. GOTCHA when scripting bulk tag deletion: `git tag -d $TAGS` with a command-substituted multiline var mangled under zsh (stray-quote, exit 128) and left a partial state — use a per-tag `for t in $(...); do git tag -d "$t"; git push origin ":refs/tags/$t"; done` loop instead (idempotent).

RECURRENCE CONFIRMED (2026-07-23, v1.3.0 cut): this clone still carried ALL 36+ purged tags locally (v0.x, old v1.4.0-v1.14.0, malformed v02.2.1-rc.1) — including a stale v1.3.0 pointing at an April codexCLI commit that a blind tag-push would have SHIPPED as Reverie v1.3.0. The Leg C stale-tag check caught it. Cleaned local-only via: for t in $(comm -23 <(git tag -l|sort) <(git ls-remote --tags origin|awk -F/ '{print $3}'|grep -v '\^{}' |sort)); do git tag -d "$t"; done. PRE-RELEASE RITUAL: run that comm check in every clone before any tag push — the old v1.4.0+ tags are future collisions for the Find/Reach/Scale releases.
